title: Zendaya Says She Felt ‘Incredibly Nervous’ While Shooting ‘The Odyssey’ but Credits Tom Holland for Supporting Her: He Was ‘in the Corner Like, “You Got This”’
description: Zendaya might be one of Gen Z’s definitive leading ladies, but even she was “incredibly nervous” while playing Athena in Christopher Nolan’s “The O
body:
Zendaya might be one of Gen Z’s definitive leading ladies, but even she was “incredibly nervous” while playing Athena in Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey.”

	“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” said the star during a recent Q&A held at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, ‘This is like, a pinch-me moment’…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, ‘I don’t want to mess this up.’”
	

	She continued: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there are so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out — so many — stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

	She credits Tom Holland, her husband and co-star (he played Telemachus, the son of Odysseus and Penelope), for easing her on-set nerves: “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” 

	All her worry was for naught, though, as Nolan told Fandango that the “Dune” actress was “always perfect.”

	Zendaya and Holland tied the knot in early 2026, according to the actress’ long-time stylist Law Roach. On the red carpet at the Actor Awards, Law told Access Hollywood that “the wedding has already happened. You missed it.” Rumors of their engagement first circulated when Zendaya was spotted at the 2025 Golden Globes ceremony wearing what appeared to be an engagement ring. Holland confirmed they were engaged later that year.
	

	But “The Odyssey” isn’t the first film set they’ve shared. The couple first met on the set of Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Homecoming,” and continued to co-star in “Spider-Man: Far From Home,” “Spider-Man: No Way Home” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” In May, Zendaya told Elle that working on the films felt like a “family affair.” “I get to go to work every day with my best friend, the person that I love,” she said. “We bring our dogs to work; it’s like a family affair. We grew up on those movies! It’s like coming home.”

schema.headline: Zendaya Says She Felt ‘Incredibly Nervous’ While Shooting ‘The Odyssey’ but Credits Tom Holland for Supporting Her: He Was ‘in the Corner Like, “You Got This”’

title: Ray Tintori, Music Video Director and Filmmaker, Dies at 43
description: Ray Tintori, who directed music videos for bands including Arcade Fire and MGMT and worked on the film “Beasts of the Southern Wild,” has died in N
body:
Ray Tintori, who directed music videos for bands including Arcade Fire and MGMT and worked on the film “Beasts of the Southern Wild,” has died in New York. The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner said the death is under investigation and the cause is unknown. 

	Tintori was one of the founders of Court 13, the filmmaking collective that made “Beasts of the Southern Wild.” He served as special effects unit director on the film which was nominated for four Oscars. 
	

	The director and screenwriter, who was the boyfriend of “Saturday Night Live” alum Heidi Gardner, also directed music videos for Chairlift, Bonnie Prince Billy, The Cool Kids, The Killers and Solange.

	Most recently, he co-directed a performance of Ethan Coen’s play “Waiting” in New York with Jordan Fish, with whom he hosted the podcast “To the White Sea” about the unproduced Coen brothers screenplay.

	In Josh Safdie’s “Marty Supreme,” Tintori had a cameo as a newsreel photographer. 

	Prior to the release of “Marty Supreme,” Tintori posted on his Instagram, “Sincere thanks to Josh Safdie, Eli Bush, and Jeremy Marks for a true dream filmmaking/acting role in Marty Supreme, shooting the black and white 16mm footage for the newsreel sequence while appearing in the film as a cameraman in the Wembley finals.

	“This was a super fun callback to the 16mm unit work that Josh, myself, Jordan Fish, Jeff Delauter, Dave MacNutt and Bob Weisz did on Ang Lee’s ‘Taking Woodstock,’ where we embedded with the cast, in costume, shooting handheld footage that was cut into the film. This time my role was Newsreel Unit Producer. I worked again with master cinematographer Ryan Marie Helfant. For certain setups we used Josh’s old crank Bolex camera that the early Red Bucket Films shorts were shot on. Ryan used an Arriflex 16SR and I operated an Arriflex 16S. Our unit also filmed the scene of Endo working in the clock factory,” he wrote.
	

	Tintori’s thesis film “Death to the Tinman” premiered at Sundance, winning a short filmmaking award. He worked in a number of different areas on various films and television shows, including acting, special effects and in the art department on projects such as “Eon Flux.”

	The son of film editor and NYU Kanbar Institute chair John Tintori and the late script supervisor Mary Cybulski, he graduated from Wesleyan University.

schema.headline: Ray Tintori, Music Video Director and Filmmaker, Dies at 43

title: CAA and Hybe Launch Strategic Partnership
description: Entertainment and sports agency Creative Artists Agency and music behemoth/lifestyle platform Hybe launched a partnership to grow Hybe’s creative a
body:
Entertainment and sports agency Creative Artists Agency and music behemoth/lifestyle platform Hybe launched a partnership to grow Hybe’s creative and commercial opportunities.

	Through Hybe’s artist network and CAA’s global reach, the companies will collaborate across content, brand partnerships, sports, live experiences and licensing and merchandising to expand Hybe’s growth in its content, brands and global IP.


	“This partnership with CAA marks an important step in expanding creative possibilities for Hybe’s artists,” said Hybe CEO Jason Jaesang Lee in a statement. “By bringing together our complementary strengths and global networks, we aim to extend the reach and value of our artists and their IP across content, brands and live experiences. Together, we will explore new creative opportunities that transcend borders and formats, bringing audiences closer to our artists through more immersive and meaningful experiences.”
	

	The partnership also aims to accelerate strategic and commercial initiatives across Hybe’s key markets, which includes Korea, Japan, the Americas, China and India.

	“Hybe has created a cultural movement,” said Bryan Lourd, the CEO and co-chairman of CAA. “Hybe artists do not just entertain; they connect with audiences in extraordinary and innovative ways that define the future of our industry and the intersection of art, influence and fandom. We are honored to help carry that forward, building on CAA’s experience and relationships across the region, to show the world what is possible when two organizations that believe in creative talent come together.”
	

	Earlier this month, BTS’ world tour pushed Hybe to its highest quarterly revenue and operating profit in its history. Revenue for the third quarter totaled $1.13 billion with an operating profit of $140.2 million.

schema.headline: CAA and Hybe Launch Strategic Partnership

title: Jennifer Lawrence Reunites With ‘Hunger Games’ Co-Star Josh Hutcherson at ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ World Premiere
description: Jennifer Lawrence staged a “Hunger Games” reunion with co-star Josh Hutcherson at the world premiere of “Sunrise on the Reaping” in New York City.
body:
Jennifer Lawrence staged a “Hunger Games” reunion with co-star Josh Hutcherson at the world premiere of “Sunrise on the Reaping” in New York City. The two original stars of “The Hunger Games” franchise walked the red carpet and posed for photos more than a decade after the press tour for “The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2” concluded their four-movie run.

	The “Sunrise on the Reaping” world premiere turned out to be a reunion of sorts for the entire “Hunger Games” franchise. Former cast members such as Elizabeth Banks (Effie Trinket), Amandla Stenberg (Rue), Jena Malone (Johanna Mason) and Willow Shields (Primrose Everdeen) made appearances on the carpet. Rachel Zegler also posted for photos after headlining the previous prequel movie, “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” as Lucy Gray Baird, as did her co-star Tom Blyth, who played a young President Snow. 
	

	Variety reported last December that Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson were returning as Katniss and Peeta Mellark for a scene in “Sunrise on the Reaping,” so it’s no surprise the duo walked the carpet at the world premiere. Lawrence then let it slip on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast last month that Woody Harrelson would also be back as Haymitch.


	“Sunrise on the Reaping” centers on a young Haymitch (played by Joseph Zada) as he competes in the 50th Hunger Games. Book readers know that Suzanne Collins’ “Sunrise on the Reaping” novel ends with a flash-forward epilogue featuring Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch, so it appears the film adapatation is following suit.
	

	“It was unbelievable,” Lawrence said on the podcast about reprising Katniss. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him. And with Josh [Hutcherson] and Woody [Harrelson] … it was so emotional. Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful. And Woody, obviously, came through the window of my hotel room uninvited. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries or used a door.”

	In the hours leading up to the world premiere, Lawrence made headlines for sharing on her Instagram story a handful of throwback photos from her time on the press tours for the “Hunger Games” movies. The photos featured the actor alongside Hutcherson and Liam Hemsworth as they traveled across the world.

	As Katniss, Lawrence headlined four “Hunger Games” movies between 2012 and 2015. The franchise (which also includes the Rachel Zegler-led 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”) has grossed $3.3 billion to date at the worldwide box office.

	Lawrence told Variety during her “No Hard Feelings” press tour in 2023 that she was “totally” open to reprising her “Hunger Games” role of Katniss Everdeen should the right opportunity arise. She added at the time, “If Katniss ever could ever come back into my life, 100 percent.”

	See photos from the premiere below.

title: ‘NAZA’ Filmmakers Grateful for ‘Light Being Shone’ on Their Film Through Awards Conversation but Prioritize Impact: It’s a ‘Small Cog in a Machine of Resistance’
description: Over the last few years, leading documentary festival IDFA has become a crucial stop on the awards season trail, with major streamers and key studi
body:
Over the last few years, leading documentary festival IDFA has become a crucial stop on the awards season trail, with major streamers and key studios courting voters in Amsterdam’s imposing 17th-century canalside houses and theaters. One of the key titles in this year’s best documentary race, however, has foregone glitzy cocktails and receptions in favor of a lengthy on-stage conversation, with the team behind “NAZA” filling the DeLaMar theater on a rainy Monday night to discuss how the film “broke the mold” in terms of finding audiences.
	

	The panel saw a rare public appearance by director Yuval Abraham, who connected via Zoom from London, where he continues to tackle his journalism work for “NAZA” producer The Guardian, represented on the IDFA stage by editorial director, film and TV and head of documentaries Lindsay Poulton. Abraham and Poulton were joined by the film’s producer James Wilson (“The Zone of Interest”) and Fionnuala Jamison, managing director of major sales agent MK2. Rachel Szor, who directed the film alongside Abraham, was not present.

	Asked about how it feels to tackle the overwhelming calendar of a high-profile awards campaign for a film as sensitive and somber as “NAZA,” Abraham said the thought is not at the forefront of his mind. “We have so much to do with the film and also with the journalism. We’re working on the investigative journalism, and I really want to focus on that.”

	Abraham has very recent experience with the frenzy of the awards race, having won the best documentary Oscar two years ago for “No Other Land,” co-directed with Szor and Palestinian directors and activists Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal. “The awards are important in a sense because they do give more visibility, and of course, that’s what we want,” he said. “But on the other hand, my experience with ‘No Other Land’ has been that voters are also smart. They know the film is out there and they can watch it and make up their own mind.”
	

	“I prefer to focus on doing conversations with audiences when we feel it’s meaningful,” added the director. “We’re planning to be physically present to meet audiences. We hope to screen the film in front of politicians all over the world, to leverage this streaming moment when it comes out on The Guardian, when Israelis and Palestinians are able to watch it online and access it, to get people to write about it and talk about it. For me, that’s the focus.”

	Wilson echoed that thought, noting how Yuval and Szor could not be physically present in Amsterdam for the talk—or to meet with voters in the Amsterdam awards stop—because “the journalism is ongoing and they are deep in that. The killing is ongoing.”

	The veteran producer, who has a career spanning over three decades, noted how he has only recently been involved in films that have received awards attention: Jonathan Glazer’s Oscar-winning “The Zone of Interest” and Kaouther Ben Hania’s Oscar-nominated “The Voice of Hind Rajab.”

	“For me, it’s a very simple contract in a way,” he said, adding that “awards are a form of a light being shone on your film. It’s a form of marketing.” The producer then noted that awards also bring to attention films in “an era and an age where there is so much competition for attention and cinema is no longer the kind of jewel at the top of the cake, the summit of moving pictures.”



	

					‘NAZA’ team at IDFA 
	



	When prodded about the lesson behind the success of “NAZA”—which has topped 1.5 million admissions worldwide and reached a $14 million box office so far—Wilson said it is “a clarion call to distributors to not be afraid of the subject matter and to open doors to it. Because when the doors are open, people come into the cinemas to see it. People who are trying to stymie that, like the people who didn’t want to release ‘No Other Land,’ should be ignored.”

	The producer was referring to how “No Other Land” struggled to get distribution in the U.S., with the filmmaking team eventually self-distributing. That experience, Abraham noted, taught him and Szor “how long it can take for a film to be accessible to wide audiences,” something they thought about at length when discussing the release strategy for their follow-up.
	

	“NAZA” was a complete mystery until it was announced as a late addition to the Venice Film Festival competition on Aug. 24. Mere days later, it played to massive acclaim at the festival, landing a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation and winning the Special Jury Prize. During the talk, Jamison revealed the filmmakers originally intended for the film to be made available online on The Guardian the day after the festival premiere, a strategy they eventually changed after lengthy conversations with Wilson and the MK2 team.

	While the film is still scheduled to be made available online for free at The Guardian sometime in December, MK2 has secured deals for theatrical exhibition in 56 territories. In the U.S., Neon acquired it following an initial rollout by the British news company and the French sales agent.

	“Our north star with ‘NAZA’ has always been about impact. It’s how you reach people, move people, and get them talking and to be in dialogue with really important matters that are at the core of this subject. Sitting in a cinema has been an important part of that,” added Poulton of the strategy, with Abraham adding that he learned from his team that “the film being immediately accessible doesn’t necessarily translate to maximum impact.”



	

					‘NAZA’
									Courtesy MK2
	



	Releasing “NAZA” has been a particularly challenging process given the secrecy and sensitivity surrounding the project. Because the filmmakers could “only approach people [they] trusted,” that narrowed financing avenues and possible creative partners. But Wilson is quick to add that the team’s decision not to show the film to industry peers before Venice was strictly tied to security. “There was no sort of sleight-of-hand mystery to the late announcement, and I’ve heard chatter about that.”

	As for the real-life impact of the film, Abraham spoke about the “violent” reaction to the film in his home country of Israel, which did not come as a shock. One of the hardest parts, however, was dealing with the effect it had on the directors’ families. “Rachel’s parents had these right-wing protests or mobs outside her house.”

	When asked if “NAZA” had changed the way the world is dealing with the ongoing “genocide” in Gaza, Wilson said he sees cinema as “an antidote to fear and the antidote to complicity in the crime,” but that he could “make no claims” for the film singlehandedly being responsible for any responses to the conflict, but that the film spoke to people’s moral and ethical compasses.
	

	“It’s sort of interesting to look at the midterm elections in the U.S. and these swathes of candidates being successful who have come out against the mass killing, the ethnic cleansing, the genocide, but also on other issues and [mobilizing] against other forms of authoritarian hegemony, mergers, and things like that,” he said. “I like to think ‘NAZA’ is a small cog in a machine of resistance.”

schema.headline: ‘NAZA’ Filmmakers Grateful for ‘Light Being Shone’ on Their Film Through Awards Conversation but Prioritize Impact: It’s a ‘Small Cog in a Machine of Resistance’

title: ‘Reasonable Doubt’ Renewed for Season 5 Ahead of Season 4 Finale
description:
“Reasonable Doubt” has been renewed for Season 5 at Hulu and Onyx Collective, Variety has confirmed. 

	The news comes just ahead of the legal dram
body:
“Reasonable Doubt” has been renewed for Season 5 at Hulu and Onyx Collective, Variety has confirmed. 

	The news comes just ahead of the legal drama’s Season 4 finale, which is scheduled to air on Nov. 24. 

	With the release of its fifth season, “Reasonable Doubt” will be one of the longest-running scripted shows on Hulu by number of seasons, behind shows like “The Handmaid’s Tale” (six seasons), “Solar Opposites” (six seasons), and “Only Murders in the Building” (sixth season coming). 
	

	Per Hulu, Season 4 is the show’s most-watched season to date, with the show having been streamed for over 150 million hours globally since its debut in 2022. 

	“Reasonable Doubt” stars Emayatzy Corinealdi, McKinley Freeman, Tim Jo, and Angela Grovey. Season 4 also saw the addition of Durrell “Tank” Babbs and Meagan Good. Morris Chestnut, Joseph Sikora and Brandee Evans also returned as recurring guest stars, with La La Anthony, Rutina Wesley, Taylor Polidore Williams, DeVaughn Nixon and Alexxis Lemire recurring. 

	The official logline for Season 4 states:

	“After a brutal attack leaves Jax’s (Corinealdi) family and newly minted law firm shaken, nothing feels certain, especially their future. With Jax’s most loyal client at the center of a spiraling media disaster, The Stewart Firm is thrust into a high-stakes battle where every move could mean survival … or collapse of the firm. As grief lingers and pressure mounts, one question looms: Can they rebuild in time, or will the cost of moving forward too quickly be everything they stand to lose?”

	“Reasonable Doubt” is created, written and executive produced by Raamla Mohamed Hunter. Kerry Washington executive produces alongside Pilar Savone for Simpson Street, Larry Wilmore for Wilmore Films, Tamara Gregory, Anton Cropper, Lena Cordina and Erika L. Johnson. Shawn Holley, Jon Leshay and Zahir McGhee serve as co-executive producers. The series hails from Onyx Collective and is produced by 20th Television.
	

	Deadline first reported the renewal.

schema.headline: ‘Reasonable Doubt’ Renewed for Season 5 Ahead of Season 4 Finale

title: Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch Bring Stand-Up, Sketch and Songs to Hilarious New York Comedy Festival Showcase
description:
Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 brought laughter, cheers and ’90s rock parodies to the New York Comedy Festival on Thursday.

	The comedians,
body:
Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 brought laughter, cheers and ’90s rock parodies to the New York Comedy Festival on Thursday.

	The comedians, who represent the funniest and most exciting rising voices in comedy, each performed a seven-minute set for a lively audience at the Venue on Music Row at the Hard Rock Hotel in Manhattan, where they also accepted awards.

	Variety TV reporter Ethan Shanfeld delivered opening remarks before introducing Caroline Hirsch, founder of the New York Comedy Festival. Rafael Espinal, the city’s media and entertainment chief, also spoke and introduced Jake Lambert, who hosted the fete.
	



	

	



	Josh Ocean Thomas kicked off the showcase with an energetic punch and jokes about growing up mixed-race and going to Christian school. Adam Friedland brought a lectern on stage and performed a partly improvised bit that involved a lengthy acceptance speech for the award he had not yet been given. And Eilise Patton performed a solo sketch, playing a Goldman Sachs executive preparing to make a difficult phone call.



	

	



	Shapel Lacey, Wally Baram, Usama Siddiquee and Olivia Carter delivered standout stand-up sets, and Kyle Gordon closed out the show with a full-band performance of his alt-rock satire “If You Break Up With Me” and the ode to nu metal “Crawl to Me,” in which he led the crowd in a NSFW chant: “Suck the dick, drink the piss.”



	

	



	The comedians accepted their awards on stage and took a class photo with Shanfeld, Hirsch and veteran comedy talent booker Louis Faranda. The performers, attendees and industry folks then headed to the rooftop bar at the Hard Rock for drinks and light bites.
	



	

	



	Variety started its 10 Comics to Watch franchise in 2000, honoring the likes of Zach Galifianakis, Maria Bamford, Patton Oswalt and Louis C.K. It’s become a prestigious industry accolade that the magazine has bestowed upon comics like Wanda Sykes, Fred Armisen, Nathan Fielder, Nate Bargatze and Nikki Glaser. Read more about Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 here.

schema.headline: Variety’s 10 Comics to Watch Bring Stand-Up, Sketch and Songs to Hilarious New York Comedy Festival Showcase

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Extended Cut Sets December Release Date in Theaters
description: The re-release of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which features footage previously left on the cutting room floor, hits theaters on Dec. 4. Tickets g
body:
The re-release of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which features footage previously left on the cutting room floor, hits theaters on Dec. 4. Tickets go on sale Nov. 19. 

	News that “Brand New Day” was returning to theaters with an extended cut first broke in late September. While audiences will have to wait another month to know everything that’s in the “Brand New Day” re-release, Rosario Dawson is set to show up somewhere in the cut. The “Ahsoka” star first revealed during a “Daredevil” fan Q&A in August that her MCU character, Claire Temple, aka Night Nurse, had a cameo in “Brand New Day,” but the scene was removed.
	

	“There’s a frame in one of the new comics that has a young Spider-Man talking to Daredevil, and they made it so that the young Spider-Man goes to PS19 in the Lower East Side, which is where I went to elementary school,” Dawson said. “So when I tell you my post was already ready with my BTS, with my grandson wearing all his Spider-Man stuff … Then I got the email that was like, ‘Yeah, nah.’”

	Dawson’s Night Nurse is a medic who helps treat injured superheroes. The character first appeared in the first season of “Daredevil” in 2015. Dawson reprised the role in several MCU shows, including “Jessica Jones,” “Luke Cage,” “Iron Fist” and “The Defenders.”

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” first arrived in cinemas on July 31 and skyrocketed as the summer’s biggest blockbuster success. The superhero tentpole debuted to $927 million worldwide on opening weekend and has since extended its global tally to $2.5 billion. Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film is currently the third-highest-grossing movie of all time behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion).
	

	In less than two months of release, “Brand New Day” overtook 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” as the highest-grossing domestic film in history. “The Force Awakens” set the bar at $936 million domestic, and the record stood for over a decade. “Brand New Day” snatched the crown after grossing $936.773 million in 47 days in North American cinemas. 

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” sees franchise star Tom Holland face off with a mysterious telepath and try to rebuild his life as a completely anonymous web-slinger. In the previous film, Benedict Cumberbatch’s Doctor Strange wiped the memories of the entire world so no one could remember that Peter Parker was Spider-Man. Other cast members include Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jon Bernthal, Jacob Batalon, Mark Ruffalo, Tramell Tillman and Florence Pugh.

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Extended Cut Sets December Release Date in Theaters

title: The Brit List: Coming-of-Age Drama and Cornwall Crime Series Top 2026 Lineup of Best Unproduced Scripts
description:
The Brit List, the annual list of unproduced British film and TV screenplays, has revealed its 2026 lineup.

	Compiled from recommendations by the
body:
The Brit List, the annual list of unproduced British film and TV screenplays, has revealed its 2026 lineup.

	Compiled from recommendations by the British industry, 13 projects — each requiring a minimum of 10 recommendations — made it onto this year’s list. Leading the pack were Gemma Addy’s coming-of-age drama feature “Dig for Victory” and Archie Thomson’s family crime sage series “Petroc,” both with 25. 


	Previous writers on the list have included the likes of Emerald Fennell, James Graham, Abi Morgan, Jack Thorne and Peter Straughan, while the projects from the screenplays have gone on to make $2 billion at the international box office and generate more than 130 award nominations, including 6 Oscar, 16 BAFTA and 5 Golden Globe wins.
	

	Alongside the lineup, this year The Brit List has also announced Disney+ as its headline sponsor. 

	“In 2026, The Brit List and Disney+ will go further than ever before to support the great British writing talent of the future,” said Brit List founder and director Alexandra Arlango. “We look forward to introducing this year’s writers to the team at Disney+ and to our returning partners, Audible and the Film Distributors Association.”

	See the 2026 Brit List below: 

	TWENTY FIVE RECOMMENDATIONS“Dig For Victory” by Gemma Addy (The Artists Partnership)Producers: AvailableForm: Feature Film Genre: Coming-of-Age DramaSummary: In rural Wiltshire, an isolated girl comes of age in the closing months of World War II. But when a violent incident interrupts a new friendship with an older woman, she uncovers a series of secrets that will shape a deadly future.
	

	“Petroc” by Archie Thomson (Curtis Brown)Producers: About Premium Content / BosenaForm: TV Genre: CrimeSummary: When a charismatic and volatile Cornish outlaw returns home after twelve years in prison, he sets about reclaiming what he believes has been taken from his family, transforming the Penrose’s from small-time crooks into a rising criminal power. Set against the wild Cornish coastline, PETROC is a propulsive family crime saga about loyalty, belonging and identity, and the devastating consequences that follow when the past refuses to stay buried.

	TWENTY TWO RECOMMENDATIONS“Do No Harm” by Polly Findlay (Casarotto Ramsay)Producers: Hinterland Pictures / Fable PicturesForm: Feature Film Genre: ThrillerSummary: Anna, a young doctor, accepts a voluntary night shift away from her family on Christmas Eve. When her mentor, Dr. Petersen, is called away, Anna is left in charge of an overstretched maternity ward. With the pressure mounting, she has to make a series of urgent critical decisions way beyond her experience. Just as things seem to be under control, Anna realises that she’s made a tiny and very human error that may end up costing a patient her life.

	EIGHTEEN RECOMMENDATIONS“Mrs. X” by Rían Smith (Independent Talent Group)Producers: AvailableForm: TV Genre: Psychological ThrillerSummary: When details of her secret affair show up in a student’s homework, an English teacher must do battle with a mysterious blackmailer in this cat-and-mouse game that soon escalates to murder. MRS. X is a twisty-turny thriller, where our lead characters – a tense-but-warm sister pairing – are always racing against the clock, trying to get one step ahead (while always being ten steps behind). The show interrogates whether we have truly thrown off the shackles of conservative thinking, or if the societal need to control others – especially women – still bubbles under the surface …

	FIFTEEN RECOMMENDATIONS“The Trolley Problem” by Polly Cavendish (Independent Talent Group)Producers: ImaginariumForm: Feature Film Genre: Psychological ThrillerSummary: Young married couple Nick and Georgie are involved in a horrific accident in which a stranger dies. Years later, the decisions they made during those fateful moments come back to haunt them.

	“15 Summers” by Courttia Newland (Dench Arnold)Producers: Joi ProductionsForm: Feature Film Genre: DramaSummary: Dimes is a successful rapper whose pursuit of fame estranges him from his teenage son, Tristian. When Tristian joins Dimes on tour, father and son are forced into close proximity, exposing resentment, disappointment and misunderstanding. As Tristian witnesses the contradictions of his father’s world – glamour, violence and chaos – Dimes sees the young man his son is. But when a night out turns violent and Tristian is harmed, Dimes finally confronts the life he has chosen. Over one transformative summer, both must decide whether it’s too late for them – and whether Dimes can put his son before everything.
	

	THIRTEEN RECOMMENDATIONS“The Royal No One” by Levi Scott (Curtis Brown)Producers: AvailableForm: TV Genre: Comedy DramaSummary: A star finance graduate with severe social anxiety discovers that secretly selling cocaine at the nightclub where he works as a busboy boosts his confidence far more than his medication. Unbeknownst to him, the club is run by gangsters who soon coerce him into becoming their in-house dealer.

	TWELVE RECOMMENDATIONS“The Lambeth Worm” by Bec Boey (The Agency)Producers: Joi Productions/BFIForm: Feature Film Genre: HorrorSummary: Inspired by a traditional folklore tale from the writer’s native Northeast England, The Lambeth Worm tells the story of two young BESEA women who find a small creature in their tower block apartment. After washing it down the sink, the creature takes up residence in the building’s pipes. As fear spreads though the apartment block the other inhabitants become increasingly hostile and toxic, and a culture of terror and blame begins to take hold.

	“Baboons” by Alfie Flewitt (Independent Talent Group)Producers: House ProductionsForm: TV Genre: Comedy DramaSummary: The funeral of his younger brother Ernie brings Ned back to his East Midlands family home. As he and his parents grapple with their grief, they go from being a broken family to a healed one, finding love, pain, and a stray baboon along the way …

	“Hello Stranger” by Rory Platt (Curtis Brown)Producers: AvailableForm: TV Genre: Comedy Drama/ThrillerSummary: When an outlaw on the run gets stranded in a sleepy Welsh village, the locals fall prey to her charms, lies … and crimes. A female-led, Western-flavoured crime thriller: Far From the Madding Crowd meets The Good, The Bad & The Ugly.

	“Grey Matter” by Theo Toksvig-Stewart (Knight Hall)Producers: AvailableForm: Feature Film Genre: Psychological Near-Fi ThrillerSummary: In near-future London, humanoid care robot Blanche, built to nurse and programmed to forget, is taught to feel by her patient’s son. 	ELEVEN RECOMMENDATIONS“Pegged” by Rachel Tookey (The Artists Partnership)Producers: AvailableForm: TV Genre: RomcomSummary: A brocaster hiding his submissive streak. title: The Next Bond Girl: From Zendaya to Florence Pugh, 19 Actresses Who Could Join Robert Pattinson
description:
Nov 16, 2026 1:31pm PT	
	

	
		The Next Bond Girl: From Zendaya to Florence Pugh, 19 Actresses Who Could Join Robert Pattinson
body:
Nov 16, 2026 1:31pm PT	
	

	
		The Next Bond Girl: From Zendaya to Florence Pugh, 19 Actresses Who Could Join Robert Pattinson
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Getty
	

		
	
				

	The name is Pattinson, Robert Pattinson, but who will be his first Bond Girl?

	Amazon MGM Studios has made it official, naming the 40-year-old Brit the next James Bond in the exclusive franchise, with Denis Villeneuve helming the next film from a script by Steven Knight and Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing.

	But 007 is only as good as the women standing next to him, and the franchise has included some memorable (as well as some less memorable) selections over the years. Some of those the classics include Ursula Andress’ Honey Ryder in “Dr. No” (1962), Diana Rigg’s Teresa di Vicenza in “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service” (1969) and Honor Blackman’s Pussy Galore in “Goldfinger” (1964), as well as more recent standouts such as Michelle Yeoh’s Wai Lin in “Tomorrow Never Dies” (1997), Eva Green’s Vesper Lynd in “Casino Royale” (2006) and the most recent, Léa Seydoux, who was Madeleine Swann in both “Spectre” and “No Time To Die” (2021).

	The Bond girl (should it evolve to Bond Woman?) is a staple of the franchise. When James Bond was created by author Ian Fleming, many speculated that Fleming’s lover, Muriel Wright, may have been an inspiration for the female characters.

	Villeneuve gives us serious reason for optimism, as he has helped shepherd powerful roles for female characters such as Amy Adams in “Arrival,” Emily Blunt in “Sicario” and Rebecca Ferguson and Zendaya in the “Dune” franchise.

	Now that the tux has a new owner, the fun part can begin.

	Variety lists the best potential Bond girls we’d like to see in the Pattinson iteration.


			
			
	Adria Arjona
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Warner Bros.				
					
				

	Few actors have built a stronger case for a license to kill in 2026 than Adria Arjona. The Puerto Rico-born star plays a battle-hardened Army sniper in “Onslaught,” Adam Wingard’s A24 actioner, joins James Gunn’s DC Universe as Maxima in “Man of Tomorrow” and plays an FBI agent chasing Michael B. Jordan in Amazon MGM’s “The Thomas Crown Affair.” That last one is practically an audition for the studio. After proving in “Hit Man” that she can seduce and outwit a leading man in the same scene, she’s the femme fatale this franchise has been missing.

	–Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Emily Blunt
			
										
					Image Credit: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images				
					
				

	Villeneuve has already shown what Emily Blunt can do with a gun. “Sicario” made her FBI agent Kate Macer the moral center of a brutal cartel thriller, and she’s heading back into that morally murky world for “Sicario 3.” Add “Edge of Tomorrow,” the “A Quiet Place” films and Steven Spielberg’s alien thriller “Disclosure Day” and the Oscar nominee has more genre mileage than almost anyone on this list. Monica Bellucci proved in “Spectre” that a Bond woman doesn’t need to be 25. Make Blunt the seasoned MI6 veteran who has watched too many 007s come and go.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Gemma Chan
			
										
					Image Credit: Emma McIntyre/WireImage				
					
				

	Gemma Chan is technically already part of the Bond universe. In the video game “007 First Light,” she plays Dr. Selina Tan, a brilliant academic with a background in psychology and game theory whose role at MI6 is critical in Bond’s journey to earning 00 status. Now make it canon on the big screen. The British star of “Crazy Rich Asians,” “Eternals” and “The Creator” has the cool authority this franchise runs on, whether she’s behind a desk at Vauxhall Cross or across a baccarat table in Macau. She’d make a natural new M or the next Vesper.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Marion Cotillard
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Bond has a long history of casting French actors as both seductive allies and adversaries. So who better to bring a fresh French intrigue to 007’s world than Oscar-winning Marion Cotillard? The French star has already mastered seduction and deception in Robert Zemeckis’ spy thriller “Allied,” opposite Brad Pitt and proved she can hold her own in a blockbuster like Christopher Nolan’s “Inception,” starring alongside Leonardo DiCaprio. Cotillard and Robert Pattinson previously missed the chance to share the screen 15 years ago after Cotillard dropped out of “Cosmopolis.” At 51, she would also bring a welcome twist to the franchise’s tradition of casting younger love interests.

	— Elsa Keslassy

		
			
			
	Chase Infiniti
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Tribeca Festiva				
					
				

	Chase Infiniti is named after Nicole Kidman’s “Batman Forever” character, Chase Meridian, so pairing her with the current Bruce Wayne practically writes itself. The case goes deeper than trivia, though. The former kickboxing trainer stood her ground against Leonardo DiCaprio in her film debut, “One Battle After Another” and earned a BAFTA nomination for leading actress along with a Golden Globe nod. She has called performing in a major action film a lifelong dream. Make her a rookie MI6 operative or, better yet, the agent sent to replace him.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Lily James
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	A “Downton Abbey” alum, James has credits across film, TV and theater and playing a Bond Girl would be the major career breakthrough to skyrocket her career. She has shown off her singing chops in “Cinderella” and “Mamma Mia 2,” warmed hearts as love interests in “Baby Driver” and “Yesterday,” then subsequently broke those hearts in “The Iron Claw.” James Bond would be her first big-budget franchise, and James seems ready for it.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Gugu Mbatha-Raw
			
										
					Image Credit: James McCauley/Variety				
					
				

	Gugu Mbatha-Raw has done British espionage before, with early guest spots on the BBC’s spy drama “Spooks.” Since then, the Oxford-born actor has shown she can play intellect and menace with equal conviction. Her credits include the title role in “Belle,” in addition to the TVA villain Ravonna Renslayer in Disney+’s Marvel series “Loki” and Apple TV’s psychological thriller “Surface,” which she also produced. Imagine that poise turned against 007. 

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Isabela Merced
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Just like Pattinson started out with “Harry Potter” and “Twilight,” Merced had her Hollywood coming-of-age in movies like “Transformers” and “Dora the Explorer.” Then she started kicking xenomorph ass in “Alien: Romulus” and killing clickers in “The Last of Us.” Most recently, she debuted as the high-flying, mace-wielding hero Hawkgirl in “Superman” and she’ll be back in next year’s “Man of Tomorrow.” Though she’s 15 years younger than Pattinson, Merced’s star is on the rise and she has experience from several major franchises.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Inde Navarrette
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Every Bond era needs a discovery, and Inde Navarrette is the breakout of the year. She spent years working on The CW’s superhero drama “Superman & Lois” and Netflix’s teen drama “13 Reasons Why,” then turned the horror hit “Obsession” into a star-making showcase. Hollywood noticed. She has since landed the role of Rogue in Marvel’s “X-Men,” and she’ll star in and executive produce Apple’s sci-fi thriller “The Waffle House Index.” Cast her as a young field agent with something to prove, and she could do for this era what Léa Seydoux did for Daniel Craig’s.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Lupita Nyong’o
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Lupita Nyong’o was already in an epic with Pattinson earlier this year with “The Odyssey.” The Oscar-winning actress from “12 Years a Slave” (2013) also has spy experience. Her Nakia in “Black Panther” is a Wakandan undercover operative, and in “The 355″ she played a former MI6 computer specialist. She deserves a Bond role with that same double edge as an ally whose loyalty 007 the audience can never quite read.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Florence Pugh
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Imagesfor Sony Pictures				
					
				

	Pugh has fight choreography down after playing Black Widow Yelena Belova in the Marvel Cinematic Universe across several movies, so she could go toe-to-toe with Bond. Playing a Bond girl who can hold her own in a fight with a supervillain’s henchmen seems like a perfect role for Pugh. And she’ll share the screen with Pattinson in “Dune: Part 3,” so they already have a head start on their chemistry.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Margaret Qualley
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Qualley put herself on the Bond map when she danced on stage at the Academy Awards for the telecast’s tribute to the franchise in 2025. Just watching her performance, clad in a bright red dress with tuxedoed men, it was impossible not to imagine her tangoing with Bond or waltzing at a black-tie gala in a 007 movie. A trained dancer, Qualley will show off her moves as Adele Astaire in the Fred Astaire biopic and she’ll get a taste of the spy life in next year’s “Possession” remake.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Margot Robbie
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Margot Robbie has already played the con artist in “Focus,” the scene-stealer in “The Wolf of Wall Street” and the agent of chaos Harley Quinn. A Bond film would be the logical next heist. She’s fresh off playing Catherine Earnshaw opposite Jacob Elordi’s Heathcliff in “Wuthering Heights.” An untitled “Ocean’s Eleven” prequel is in development with her name attached, so she’s clearly in a caper state of mind. Picture her as a high-society villain with a twinkle in her eye and a blade in her clutch. 

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Anna Sawai
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Sam Mendes directed “Skyfall” and “Spectre,” and he’s now cast Anna Sawai as Yoko Ono in his Beatles films. On FX’s historical drama “Shōgun,” she became the first Japanese actress to win the Emmy for lead drama actress but her action credentials go back to “Ninja Assassin” and “F9.” Sawai can convey loyalty and menace along with some heartbreak in a single look. Isn’t that the entire job description of a great Bond woman?

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Hunter Schafer
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Not only would Hunter Schafer make history as the first trans Bond girl, she’d be a damn good one. Schafer has proven her acting skills over and over in “Euphoria” and is about to level up as one of the stars of the “Blade Runner 2099” series, which will undoubtedly have some intense action scenes. Yet she’s still at the phase where scoring a Bond role could completely catapult her career. We could totally see Schafer and Pattinson sharing flirty banter before going head-to-head against some baddies — and just imagine the looks on that press tour! 

	— Ellise Shafer

		
			
			
	Sydney Sweeney
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	As a blonde bombshell, Sydney Sweeney would be a Bond Girl no-brainer — and she just might have the action chops to match. Sweeney is a natural athlete — she trained for months and put on 30 pounds to play a fierce boxer in “Christy” — but still hasn’t starred in a true action movie unless you count Marvel flop “Madame Web.” This could be the perfect chance for her to flex that muscle. It remains to be seen if she could match Pattinson’s zany personality — but with her Jeff Bezos connection (Sweeney attended his wedding last year and he invested in her lingerie brand), she’s likely to be at the top of Amazon’s list.

	— Ellise Shafer

		
			
			
	Anya Taylor-Joy
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for Vanity Fair				
					
				

	Like Pugh, Taylor-Joy is another “Dune: Part 3” leading lady who is sure to attract some Bond Girl fan castings after people see her starring alongside Pattinson. She’s had some stunt training after starring as Imperator Furiosa in the “Mad Max: Fury Road” prequel, and she’ll anchor a major franchise next year with “The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.” And who wouldn’t want a high-stakes chess showdown between her and Bond, calling back to her “Queen’s Gambit” breakout role?

	–Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Sophie Turner
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Turner is already a major TV star thanks to “Game of Thrones,” but that hasn’t quite translated to the big screen. Playing a Bond Girl could change all that. She’s proven she can deliver a wordy monologue and give an icy stare after surviving Westeros politics in “Game of Thrones,” and she’s trained extensively to star in Prime Video’s “Tomb Raider” series as explorer Lara Croft. The Amazon MGM connection between the series and Bond is already there, giving Turner an easy jump to the spy world.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Zendaya
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Nobody has spent more screen time with Robert Pattinson this year than Zendaya. They played Emma and Charlie, an engaged couple, in A24’s “The Drama” before reuniting in Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” where Zendaya plays Athena. By the end of the year, they’ll be together with the future 007 auteur Denis Villeneuve in his epic conclusion, “Dune: Part Three.” With three films of proven chemistry, plus a director who already knows how to make her the most magnetic presence on a desert-swept screen, give her a morally slippery MI6 asset who’s never fully on Bond’s side and let the two-time Emmy winner keep everyone guessing.

	— Clayton Davis 

		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

title: Grand Canyon Small Plane Crash Kills 3
description:
Grand Canyon National Park
                          3 Dead After Missing Plane Found Destroyed
body:
Grand Canyon National Park
                          3 Dead After Missing Plane Found Destroyed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 16, 2026
                            4:28 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A missing plane that vanished near the Grand Canyon has been found wrecked ... with all three people aboard confirmed dead.
      
    
            According to the National Park Service, crews located the missing Piper Comanche aircraft and a debris field around 10:15 AM Monday in the Basin area of Grand Canyon National Park's North Rim.
      
    
      
      Missing Aircraft Located on the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park (News Release)
The National Park Service has located a downed aircraft near the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park.
The aircraft and debris field were located by NPS at approximately 10:15 a.m. on Nov. 16 in the Basin area. There were no survivors.
Grand Canyon Regional Communications Center received a report of a missing Piper Comanche aircraft with three people aboard at approximately 11:30 p.m. Nov. 15. The aircraft’s last known location was in the vicinity of the Basin area on the North Rim.
The cause of the incident will be investigated by the National Transportation Safety Board with support from the NPS.
No additional information is available, and the names of the people aboard are being withheld out of respect for the family's privacy at this time.
Additional information available: https://t.co/HYwrAolu36
              @GrandCanyonNPS
          
  
    
            The plane was first reported missing around 11:30 PM Sunday, prompting an extensive search operation ... it was last known to be in the vicinity of the Basin area with three people said to be on board.
      

            Authorities launched an aerial search early Monday morning, with the Arizona Department of Public Safety using forward-looking infrared technology and night vision to try to locate the aircraft, according to NPS. The search effort also included Coconino County Search and Rescue, Kane County Search and Rescue and the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The National Transportation Safety Board says they will investigate the crash, with assistance from the National Park Service, however it's still unclear what caused the plane to go down at this time.
      
    
            The identities of the passengers have not yet been released.

            3:13 PM PT -- United Airlines says it resolved a technology issue that affected departing flights, according to AP.
      
    
            The travel headaches just keep coming ... United Airlines is dealing with a widespread system outage Monday, leaving flights stuck on the ground just days after the FAA's rare nationwide ground stop.
      
    
            United confirmed it's experiencing a widespread system outage affecting departing flights ... throwing another wrench into travelers' plans. The airline says flights already in the air are not affected, and neither are United Express flights.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            One passenger wrote on X that her flight was grounded because of an issue with the plane's weight-and-balance system ... though she says her pilot clarified the problem was unrelated to Friday's FAA meltdown.
      
    
            As we reported ... the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop Friday after a technical malfunction disrupted air traffic control communications, bringing departures across the country to a halt.
      
    
            It's unclear how long United's latest outage will last or how many flights have been affected.
